summary: The study describes the use of atomic layer deposition (ALD) to modify the pore structure of diatom frustules by depositing an ultrathin film of titanium oxide (TiO2). The process involves sequential exposures to titanium chloride (TiCl4) and water as precursors. The ALD technique allows for controlled reduction of pore sizes while preserving the 3D shape and geometry of the diatom pores. The reduction in pore size is dependent on the number of deposition cycles, with pore diameters ranging from 40 nm to less than 5 nm. The study highlights the potential of ALD for creating highly selective membranes for molecular separation applications.
evidence: TiO2 is deposited by sequential exposures to titanium chloride (TiCl4) and water. The sequential pulsing of precursor couples at a substrate temperature of 100 uC was 0.4 s/0.5 s/0.5 s/0.5 s for the particular reaction sequence TiCl4/purge/H2O/purge. The reduction in pore size is dependent upon the number of deposition cycles. The film thicknesses obtained from inside pores were comparable with TiO2 growth rate (0.060 nm cycle−1) determined from a control experiment on silicon.
